newsitem.title: UK: Intra-Asian air cargo business to top world growth.
newsitem.headline: Intra-Asian air cargo business to top world growth.

text.p: Trade between Asian countries will continue to drive the highest regional air cargo growth rate, with an annual average of nine percent between now and 2015, Boeing Co said.
Asian air cargo growth is seen rising 15 percent in 1996, down from the 20.4 percent recorded for 1995.

In its latest World Air Cargo Forecast released here on Thursday, Boeing said that Asia's successful realisation of its economic potential through a strongly coordinated network of industrial capabilities was behind the growth of intra-Asian air freight.
Boeing said Japanese investment has paved the way for this expansion while Hong Kong, Korea, Singapore and Taiwan are also pursuing capital investment stratgies within the region.
Economic reforms in mainland China and re-emerging Vietnam will further encourage investment and trade opportunities.
It added that intra-Asia's share of the world air cargo market is expected to grow by about 60 percent by 2015 from its present eight percent share.

Trans-Pacific air cargo growth is forecast to rise by an eight percent annual average reflecting the continuing strength of the Asian economies, combined with Asia's rapidly expanding share of manufactured goods for export, Boeing said.
This is expected to represent 40 percent of the world export market by 2015, against today's level of 28 percent.
Two-way air cargo trade between Europe and Asia is forecast to rise at annual rate of 7.4 percent over the period.

Boeing said the African air cargo market is expected to grow at around five percent a year till 2015. Business with Europe is seen rising an annual average six percent and to the U.S. at five percent.

It added the Europe-Africa market demonstrated more growth than any other involving Africa in 1994 and that "evaluation of this largest African market confirms the existence of a growing market capable of generating significant additional air trade."

The Middle East market is forecast to grow at an annual average of six percent. Traffic with Asia will move slightly faster at 6.5 percent while North American trade will grow at 5.5 percent, it added.
